content.content: WHEN Enter or Shift+Enter is pressed in the search field and the selection that key press makes changes, the viewer shall bring the viewport to rest by the centring move wzsxvmvw records, carried with that move's recorded terms and with nothing added to them: the per-axis terms stay the move's own, decided by the same axis test the record draws and requiring there what the record already requires, a recorded pan limit reaches the move exactly where the record says it reaches one, and the zoom level is left unchanged as the record leaves it. This rule adds a third trigger to that one move and no second move: it states no pan, no zoom and no clamp of its own, it neither relaxes nor tightens either axis term, and it puts no viewport consequence behind the selection that the recorded move does not already carry. The node a move so triggered centres on is the node the recorded selection identifies - the node selected, and no other; which node that is stays the selection's to settle, and this rule reads no property of that selection beyond the node it identifies: not focus, not emphasis, not a drawn position. The trigger stands on its own: the selection these two key presses make in the search field starts the centring by itself, with no focus move onto the node and no activation of a listed id, so neither recorded centring trigger is read into it, narrowed to reach it or widened to cover it; whether the selection carries focus onto the node is not assumed here, and where it does, the result is the one move the recorded rule holds to be one and the same, not a second centring. Where these key presses make no selection, as where the query marks no node, the viewer shall not move the viewport: a centring move arises from a selection, and no selection is made - a consequence of this trigger, not a rule about when a selection changes. Which key presses act, in which context they act, over which set they walk, in which direction, in which order and with which wrap are yqwsztww's as recorded, and the decisions it names keep what it leaves to them, both which nodes count as marked and what the same key press does outside the search field; marking still selects nothing by itself, which is why the centring answers to the selection and not to the mark. This rule restates, narrows, widens and substitutes none of that, and it reaches neither the search field's own behaviour nor what closes it: it names the selection those key presses make and adds only where the viewport stands once that selection exists.
content.rationale:
The search's Enter and Shift+Enter walk a selection through the nodes the field's query marks (yqwsztww), and the node that walk lands on can be anywhere in the graph - off screen as easily as the node a Tab press reaches. Bringing it into view is the move the viewer already makes when it centres on a node, wzsxvmvw's, and the useful thing to do with a node the reader has just stepped onto is to show where it is. So this node adds a trigger to that one move rather than giving the search a viewport rule of its own: a centring move is a centring move however the node is named, and the axis terms, the limits and the untouched zoom level do not change because the node's name came from a key press in the field rather than from focus or an activation.

Adding to the recorded trigger set is also why nothing of the move is restated here. The fitted-axis term, the overflowing-axis term, where a recorded pan limit reaches a centring move, and the zoom level left unchanged are all wzsxvmvw's own words; a copy would be a second thing to keep true, would break the day that node is reworded, and would leave a reader unable to tell a cited term from a term settled anew. This node therefore names the move and says the recorded terms carry it - nothing added, nothing relaxed, nothing tightened - and a reader who wants to know what a term requires reads it where it is recorded. The same restraint keeps the move single: a rule stated for the search would be a second move, so the rule is stated as a trigger on the one move and the record's terms are the only terms it has.

Which node is centred is not re-derived either. wzsxvmvw already settles that a centring move centres on the node its trigger identifies, and yqwsztww settles which node the two key presses select, by walking the marked set in the recorded order with the recorded wrap, so the third trigger identifies its node through that selection and this node has nothing to add: the centred node is the selected node, and the identity of that node stays where it is decided. That is also why the rule reads no property of the selection beyond the node it identifies. Nothing records that a selection made in the search field moves focus onto the node, and a centring that waited on such a focus would hang on a property no decision states, so the trigger is stated as the selection itself, standing on its own rather than being read into the first recorded trigger's 'a means other than a pointer click on that node' or into the activation trigger. If the selection does also carry focus, wzsxvmvw holds that a move answering to both triggers is one and the same move, and the same holds here: one centring, not two.

No marked node touching nothing is kept, and it is kept without re-settling the selection. yqwsztww records that a query marking no node leaves the selection unchanged; the consequence for the viewport - nothing centred - belongs to this node, because the viewport consequence is the only thing this node adds, and it is stated as a consequence of the trigger, a centring move arising from a selection where none was made, rather than as a rule about when a selection changes. Stated the other way round it would be a second copy of yqwsztww's condition, which is exactly what the rest of this node avoids.

The remaining boundary is the selection's own. Which key presses act, in which context, over which set of nodes, in which direction, in which order and with which wrap are yqwsztww's as recorded, and the decisions yqwsztww names keep what it leaves to them: which nodes count as marked, and what the same key press does outside the search field. The marking still selects nothing by itself, so a marked node is not a selected one and the centring cannot answer to the mark; the order and the wrap are untouched, because a selection that steps from the last marked node to the first is still a selection and its centring is the same move, not a special case of it. Nor does this node reach the field's own behaviour, what closes the field, or what a graph reload does with the viewport: it reads one thing, the selection those key presses make, and adds one thing, where the viewport stands once that selection exists. The pointer carve-out wzsxvmvw keeps and the boundary it draws at a change of the panel's own focus are unchanged as well - neither a pointer click on a node's box nor a change of the panel's focus is a selection made by these two key presses, so the third trigger neither narrows nor widens either of them, and a focus that arrives or ends without a selection being made still moves no viewport by this node.
